title: Video VAEs and receptive fields
hook: How far one latent can see, measured by experiment, and why that sets the first-frame rule and the overlap your tiles need.

verified.claim: The formula for the receptive field matched autograd measurements on six stacks.
Two causal stride-2 layers gave (n - 1) // 4 + 1 frames for every length tested, the rule from the empty-latent nodes.
Wan's CausalConv3d pads only on the past side in time, with an optional cache from the previous chunk.
LTX's CausalConv3d has a causal flag in forward, so that VAE can run both ways.
The graph passes validate_prompt with file menus skipped.

unchecked: We did not measure the receptive field of a real video VAE. Real stacks add attention, up and down sampling blocks, and residual paths, so the numbers here are for plain convolution stacks.
The first version of this lesson's references to LTX-Video and HunyuanVideo paper titles and arXiv numbers were wrong and are removed. CU-215 cites the LTX-Video paper with its right title.
We have not tested how large a tile overlap each real VAE needs. The rule here is for a hard join in the middle of the overlap: the overlap should be at least twice the receptive radius.
The code gives no reason for Wan 2.2's decode estimate having no frame count. Linking it to the feature cache is our reading.
